text: Everyyyyyone told me to come to Ruby Slipper Cafe when I came back to visit NOLA once more. Why? Is a question that lingers. My friend Kirby, a NOLA Native, also suggested Ruby Slipper Cafe and then I knew that perhaps, this was a place to put on my list. With numerous locations, I feared the wait would match that of the Canal St. location where I observed crowds of guests waiting outdoors for seating. Luckily at the Broad St. location, we seemingly walked right in. Busy and filled with guests on a Sunday morning, I figured I was in for a real treat after all of the recommendations passed onto me. We were seated at a small booth in the back and awaited our waitress. After waiting about 15 minutes, we were finally greeted and placed our drink orders. 10 minutes later, we got drinks. This seemed to be the routine of the morning, as the service received was spaced out and nothign to write home about. Because Kirby and I are both former servers, we understand the pros and cons of serving and try not to be critical but were quite dissapointed that we struggled to get our servers attention despite the lack of fuss happening in her section. Despite that, we continued to focus on our meal. Kirby opted for French Toast with an extra side of Bacon, "not fried crispy, but soft" and as a pregnant woman, I know she meant this. I ordered a Croque Madame with a side of bacon as well and we waited with baited breath, hoping our meals would come fast enough to keep Kirby, the baby and myself in good spirits -- and from eating someone elses food on a neighboring table. When our food finally arrived to our table about 15-20 min. later, we were both starving and planned to dive right in. Upon review of our food as I was snapping some shots, we realized that the bacon Kirby previously requested be "not fried crispy, but soft" as her cravings desired, was almost as black as the boots I was wearing. It's almost like the server didn't pass the memo on at all. When we finally got ahold of her, we promptly sent the bacon back and continued our meals. Kirby was a big fan of her French Toast and the bacon they finally did bring out. My Croque Madame, not so much but this was my first experience trying one. I think that I expected something sweet and savory, but the bread was dryer than expected vs. being soft to the bite, although I appreciate the huge slices. Overall, my experience simply fell short of what I expected. I don't find myself loving chain food too much and believed Ruby Slipper to be different... but maybe another try will prove me wrong?
label: NEG

text: Sat down to some delicious appetizers & craft beer (the IPA is hoppin', like double down on the delicious hops). The bartender is a keen fellow, very polite and energetic with impeccable serving manners, and our trainee server was aces. Then came the main course. The lovely lady on my left had a savoury pulled pork burger (her fave) on a brioche that struggled to keep the goodness in, flanked by a mountain of fluffy fries and creamy side 'slaw. In front of me was a fragrant fantasia of fromage. I could have cried, and it wasn't the onions, because they were wrapped in a rich beef gravy-broth, square-dancing with crunchy croutons under a dome of blended cheeses that sent this french onion soup soaring to the top of the charts. Just as tasty: the cheesy mushroom burger with plenty of each, wrapped in a brioche with a leaf of lettuce so you can tell mama with a straight face that you ate your veggies. They tried to stuff some dessert down me, but it just wouldn't go; I was full of goodness, make no mistake. Tip top food for a casual establishment, good atmosphere, and not too loud on a weeknight. Thankfully few televisions, and the kind of small-town charm that lets all sorts of people mingle in comfort with great food and drink. First Impression, 5 stars, and you can bet I will be making follow-up visits, stay tuned.

text: I FINALLY made it to The Met, the GORGEOUS restored opera house, originally built in 1908 by Oscar Hammerstein. It was even more spectacular than I imagined it would be! I spent more time staring at the opulent crystal chandelier hanging in the middle of the space, glancing at all of the French Baroque details, elegant monogram "M's around the balconies, striking crown molding and secluded opera boxes (while imagining I was in Vienna or Paris), than I did looking at the stage. If attending the right kind of show here, the combination of sound and surroundings could really make for one spectacular, stunning, unforgettable night on north Broad. Who would've thought? Before I get to music, I just have to say how much I LOVED the juxtaposition between the classically decorated ballroom with the uber modern, yet still classy restrooms. The crispy white subway tiles, funky sconces and sleek brushed gold mirrors were everything. Kuddos to the interior designer. They get it. They soooooo get it!! I surprise my husband with tickets to a show here. I purchased them on a resale site for next to nothing! I did see some shows were quite a bit pricey from the venue's actual website, so I would definitely recommend grabbing them in person from the box office if possible, or pricing them out a resale site beforehand! The sound here was so incredible! The acoustics are truly fantastic! Like, unreal! We sat in the lodge and it was honestly a wonderful place to take in the entire space. I would recommend sitting up there if you want the full experience of the venue, not just being close to the stage. We had no problem seeing the stage, and in fact, I remember thinking that although the space is so large, it still felt so intimate because of how the venue was shaped (and the fact that there were no tv screens). My only gripe would be leg room was a tad lacking and I'm pretty short. The hike up to the lodge area in heels after a few cocktails was not made without effort and careful foot placement. Watch out, ladies! I will say the fact that there were restrooms up there was awesome, however. Even though the venue is quite large, it still felt intimate somehow. It was just so lovely. I honestly loved every minute of being here, even though it wasn't for my kind of music Brews were average with the "fanciest" being Goose Island. Typically overpriced but not nearly as bad as the sports complexes or other music venues. Too shelf liquor was available for cocktails. Parking is Street and there's definitely some unmetered spots. It's also very easily accessible by the subway! P.S. groupies, the tour buses are right there so chances of meeting your favorite musicians are pretty good.

text: Covid Times Thanks to my extended time on the ground in Indy, I have finally found the time to tackle my "Local Places to Visit" list. If you are Vonnegut fan, this must visit. Currently, the first floor still has a bit of construction ongoing, and coming together nicely. + The museum has three floors; however, if you are unable to navigate the stairs, there is an elevator. The first floor has the library books (including a banned books session) and what would have been some tables to sit and rest at, but thanks to Covid, they were put up. The second floor has a small gift shop, the bar/event space with patio seating outside with a 'Happy Birthday Wanda June' design, a small exhibit space , and Kurt's old typewriter. The third floor is currently exhibiting and featuring painting passed on Slaughter House Five. + The museum has a small parking lot available, as well as paid for street parking off of Indiana Ave. Tips: ***Due to Covid, the tours are restricted in size and times. I will never adopt a cat from this place again and if you are looking to do so please go somewhere else. She also explained to me that I signed a foster to adopt form but I never did any such thing. When I told her I didn't, she said it was what I signed on my phone. text: MEXICAN FOOD EMERGENCY Working on the road is not always glamorous for example my day started at 5am with breakfast at a Starbucks in Hammond, Indiana. Fast forward to midnight and I've worked all day without a proper meal. Typically I'm going to go to bed hungry because there aren't many food options on the road past 10pm, unless you want crappy fast food. I truly love my Yelp app because it's there for me during food emergencies. I'm always using my filters based on my needs. Tonight I used "Open Now" which helps me filter through my available food options. I don't need to start reading 5 star reviews about a place that is closed at midnight. That never helps and I just get HANGRY!This place immediately showed up and was only 0.9 miles from my hotel. The best part is they were even open 24/7 which also gets a lifetime bookmark from me in case of another midnight Mexican Food Emergency. When I drove up I noticed four guys eating inside which is always a good sign. Empty restaurants feel scary. I also noticed the restaurant had a drive thru too which I may use on my next visit. When I went inside my eyes got huge. Everything on the menu looked fantastic. Remember I had Starbucks for breakfast about 19 hours ago. There's a good chance I'm ordering the whole menu board. I decided to get the Steak Burrito which comes the way I totally love it with just pico de gallo and guacamole. Score! I also added on an order of the chicken enchiladas. While I was waiting for my order to be made the guy at the counter pointed me to the self serve salsa bar! I was so happy to see this. I was carrying out and I packed three salsa verde, two mild red and two hot red salsas. They even provided little lunch baggies just in case you didn't put the lid on right and it opened up on your way home. I call that Salsa Safety! On a side note another Yelper blasted this place for not having any salsa. I feel bad for them because the free self serve salsa was right in the dining room. I'm not sure how you could miss this Mecca of Salsa. I loved both the medium spicy verde and the mild red salsa. I carried out my food because it's sad to eat alone at midnight plus no one can see you pigging out in your hotel room. The steak burrito was wonderful. This is how I like it. It was so simple. Grilled steak along with fresh guac and pico wrapped in a grilled burrito is the bomb. This is the only way to have it. The chicken in the enchiladas was nice too. The white meat was shredded and moist. The red enchilada sauce was also tasty and rich. I enjoyed the salad on top too. This makes the dish healthy. Right? I would definitely come back especially for late night food. Was the food here life changing? Nope but it's good Mexican. I throughly enjoyed every bite and it saved me from going to bed or eating at a gas station. Ironically before stopping here I almost bought a ramen bowl at the gas station up the road. I'm honestly glad I didn't because this meal was much better. Desperation truly sets in when your tired and hungry. I'm glad I found this 24/7 restaurant. I will always visit you at midnight when I'm working in the area. I might even use that drive thru now that I know what to order.

text: 2 months ago we paid $4000 for peace of mind to have a snake fence installed by Arizona Snake Fence Company on our backyard preserve fence. We did not want to worry about rattlesnakes in our yard. The company advertises that they provide "post-install snake removals", "post-install inspection to meet all tolerance requirements necessary to meet a safe area", and a "free warranty"; all of which also made us feel that this was a very good investment. Initially, we felt secure in our backyard after the fence installation. Earlier this week I was frightened when I came within 1 foot of a coiled rattlesnake in our backyard! Thankfully, I was not bitten. It was on our side of the fence (see photo with snake fence behind the snake)! It should be noted that we never leave our side gate propped open, and there have been no tradesmen working in our back yard since the snake fence was installed who could have possibly "tampered" with our fence in anyway (this was the suggestion of the snake fence company's owner). Home alone, I panicked, and tried to call and email the snake fence company a few times that day to remove the rattlesnake from our yard. Unfortunately I only reached their answering machine, and had to then obtain another service to remove the snake from my backyard. The owner of the company did eventually call me back later that day, and stated that he would come out to check the fence the next day. But, at that time (even before visualizing the fence in person) he suggested possible causes other than fault with their fence installation. When he did come to my home to check the fence the next day, he pushed down some fencing wire with pliers, that I had pointed out to him of openings that looked large enough for a snake to slide through. He did this along 3 - 4 grout line areas under the fence, where the fence bottom meets the block wall. He at first said that the snake could have possibly entered in those small opening areas. Later in the conversation, he stated that he thought that the snake could have been actually hiding in our yard for the last 2 months (prior to them doing the fence), and they "may have missed it during the fence installation", or that our side gate had been left open too long by someone to allow the snake to enter from the front yard and the road, because he didn't actually think it came in through from the backyard preserve through the small identified openings below the fence that I had pointed out to him. He also stated that he didn't see any "tampering" by others of my fence. My husband and I were then floored when he charged us a service call for the visit! The company touts a "free 1 year warranty" on their website. But I was told that even after spending $4000 just two months ago for his services, that our request for him to come out post-install after a live rattlesnake showed up in our yard to assess our safety, the security of the fence, and to restore our peace of mind was not covered under the free "warranty". We are very disappointed in the customer service (or lack of) that was provided by the owner of Arizona Snake Fence.

The last thing we tried was the miso cauliflower. I only had a few bites of this because I was already so full, but the flavor was great. I'm always amazed how good cauliflower can be. text: Two years ago, tiki bars where *everywhere*... except Nashville. The trend may have come and gone but, I think, Nashville is going to have many fun nights ahead at Chopper. Its emergence was long-discussed and going by the wait times its brought since opening, people have wanted this for a while. If you're unaware, the bar sits in the old Bar Luca spot -- and it's entirely unrecognizable. There's plenty of bamboo, robots and tiki touches to make the space its own and not harken back to what it was before. There are a perimeter of booths (require a 'reservation' or for your name to be on a list; at this point you can't just sit down in one) and the bar takes up the middle of the, er, bar. The bar has attached stool/seats so idle up where you fit in and get to it. Food's coming but right now Chopper is all about the tiki. Some drinks are classics. Some are riffs off classics. My drink choices were a hit and miss but, I think, that depends on who makes your drink. The staff is new. The bar is new. The menu is new. People are still trying to get a feel for what's going on. As such, your mileage may vary with drink and bartender. I started with the Chopper Mai Tai. I've many a Mai Tai'd in my day. I did not care for this. At all. My buddy (who was all in on his Caribbean Punch) did not like it. I don't think that I wasn't picking up what the twist was putting down. I just don't think it was made right. It didn't taste like any Mai Tai I've ever had. Ever. The only saving grace of it was that it was super boozy. Cocktails run $11-$14 here but you get your money's worth. I could have breathed fire from my first sips. Wanting to give the drinks another shot, I went with a classic Tiki drink: the Jet Pilot. This was made by the bartender who made my buddy's drink and it was a success. They told me it would cost $25 per person for a meal that, on any other Sunday, would have been much less - although they did throw in a beverage and a muffin or fruit cup... So, when we got there, they had packed the small place with too many tables, most of which had families seated at them. Our waiter even commented on the "close quarters." We got our beverages and "complimentary" muffins, danishes and fruit cups. Our breakfast order was taken about twenty minutes after arrival. And we didn't receive our food until an hour and fifteen minutes after arrival. (Let that sink in for a moment...) Tables whose orders were taken after ours got their food before us, too. When it did arrive, the food was mediocre and lacking in flavor. Our waiter came out towards the end to commiserate about how busy they were and apologize for the slow service. He then made a comment that the next seating would not be allowed any modifications to menu items. (Our table had asked for a couple of minor modifications to the meals - i.e. "no tomatoes" - so this was obviously aimed at us.) We heard other tables complaining about the food and service. It's really a shame that a restaurant that people seem to like (based on the positive reviews) would try to capitalize on Mother's Day by over-charging and over-stuffing the restaurant with too many customers at once, putting a strain on the kitchen and servers and causing sub-par food to be served unacceptably slowly. I will not be returning.
label: NEG

Gooey-ness from the white cheddar (that's what she said). And a little spice from the arugula. Everything is perfect together. Just like Matthew Perry and Salma Hayak in Fools Rush In. You bite. You bite. You devour it and now there's nothing left except the grease along the rim of your mouth. You thank BM for the BDSM Burger and a good time. You even leave them the tip. (Not that tip.) Latte was fine, but nothing exceptional - if anything, it was a little weak. I went back to the counter for food, and asked what's good, and what's the soup? The gentleman behind the counter encouraged me to try the soup - "a beef stew," he said at least twice. I ordered a cup and paid - at least it didn't cost as much as my latte - and he brought me a bowl of something that was neither beef nor stew. It was an okay soup with slices of smoked sausage (reminded me of the Eckert's that my mom used to buy shrink-wrapped - nothing special) and lots of white beans. It had a thin, lightly tomatoey broth that was nearly clear. No beef, no potatoes, no thick stewy goodness. Very disappointing. The space itself is quirky and welcoming, with plenty of room to study quietly or gather with a group. The staff members I encountered were friendly. I appreciate Stone Spiral's place in the community as a venue fo art and music, and hope they get a consistent menu and pricing in place soon.

text: STRONG CAUTION AGAINST USING THIS FACILITY! Although there may have been a few positive highlights, the majority of the experience that my family had with Casas Adobes Post Acute Rehabilitation (Skilled Nursing Facility) was absolutely AWFUL! To be clear, my mother was discharged from the hospital to this facility during COVID, therefore I understand the need for no visitors. However, with that being the case, one would think that the communication between the staff and the patient's families would be of the utmost priority, which it most certainly was NOT. Especially considering the fact that the patient has communication issues due to previous strokes and has a diagnosis of mild cognitive impairment - that makes it even more important to COMMUNICATE WITH THE FAMILY! In addition to the communication being a major issue, my 90 lb. mother fell THREE TIMES while in the care of this facility...even though she was marked as a fall risk in the hospital. I still do not understand how that can happen! Furthermore, she lost her partial one-tooth denture during the first week of her stay. After trying to figure out what happened or how they could replace it, I was basically told that there was nothing they could do. Coupled with the utter lack of communication, the processes of rehabilitation, therapy, discharge, and transfer to an assisted living facility were not broken down or explained to our family at all. We were consistently given the runaround, calls and emails were not returned, and the process was made a lot more stressful than I believe it needed to be. In addition, one family member needed to provide documentation to his employer in order for his leave time to be approved for helping to handle my mother's affairs. The staff at Casas Adobes led us to believe that it would be no problem to have that filled out; yet after having the paperwork for TWO WEEKS, it was returned to us incomplete, causing our family member to be penalized. If I have learned anything while advocating for my mother, it is that I wish there had been more reviews like this when I was researching facilities for her. My family and I chose Casas Adobes from the short list of rehab centers the hospital provided us with, because it seemed as though they would be able to meet my mother's needs and the public generally had positive experiences to report. After digging a little deeper, I can see that many positive reviews for this facility are over 3 years old. Clearly the quality has gone downhill! Following my first-hand experience at this facility, I must say that I would not recommend that anyone send his or her loved ones here. There are a few great workers here (mainly the two ladies at the front desk who had to put up with my incessant calling to try to get my questions answered), but the competence of the facility as a whole was completely unacceptable. I would not wish this added stress upon anyone, especially during a time when most people navigating this territory are already struggling to deal with the illness of a family member or loved one. I would strongly advise that you PICK ANOTHER FACILITY!

text: Stay here if you have *any* opportunity to do so. There are lots of reasons I make such an unqualified recommendation--here are mine (as a function of three recent stays for three weeks worth). As a frequent traveller for work to a variety of places, it is a genuine value to come to a place that is visually pleasant, not only in the lobby, but in the room. Usually the places that have this kind of charm and interest are boutique, older properties that come with the penalties of such age. But Hotel St Louis is a place that is the former, but nit the latter. It has been completely and recently renovated from its historic use as a bank headquarters. That renovation was notably well done and provides a hotel that has classic charm but the desired elements of a well noise-isolated room, HVAC comfort, and a nice bathroom (some people emphasize the fancy toilets, but it is their wonderful showers that I find the more important). Likewise, the staff is genuinely friendly and effective. The check in staff clearly has a vision to make each person feel individually engaged--it is a notable difference and speaks to the character this hotel seeks to convey and build as an experience throughout your stay (with a shout-out on this note due to "Thanos"). There is a blemish to be worked out on the housekeeping side (two of my three stays involved a housekeeping issue noticed on my arrival), but the management made things right with no undue prompting. So I saved the best for last--the in-hotel restaurant, Union 30. They have a craft bartender, Lucas, that is rightfully being recognized by Marriott national for his elegant approaches and outstanding execution. The onsite chef is clearly combining top-shelf ingredients with delicious vision and awesome execution--the food is remarkably good. Ordinarily I consider eating at the hotel restaurant as a sign that I worked too late and ran out of energy to get to the good places to eat that I very much value--but I was thrilled to discover that I didn't have to go any further than my lobby for great meals. And I found myself sitting next to more locals coming there to eat than any other hotel restaurant I've ever been to. Given the long hours I often work, having the opportunity to have a great meal served by great staff in a great setting is a real difference that is why I'm starting my third stay and have booked to come back for when my work brings me back to St Louis in a couple of weeks.
label: POS

text: My husband's family is from Peru so we frequent Machu Picchu on the west side and Don Juan's Sandwiches quite often. Both restaurants changed ownership from Peruvian families to other Latin American families in the past 2-4 years, which made us concerned that the food quality would go down. I'm happy to say Don Juan's survived the switch! Our family normally shares an appetizer of Salchipapa (sliced hot dogs, fries, all covered in ketchup, mustard, and mayo), and I normally order El Desayuno Don Juan (Don Juan's Breakfast), a classic Peruvian breakfast that is so big, it's pretty much my lunch and dinner. It comes with sliced chicharron (pork), sliced camote (sweet potato), red onions, bread, and a tamale. You can ask for relleno (blood sausage) as well, and stuff all of that into the bread to make a sandwich, topped with aji (spicy sauce). My favorite sandwich is the torta de pescado (fish sandwich) but lomo saltado (juicy beef, tomatoes, and onions) is really good as well. Don't forget the ceviche! Yes, the owner is the cook for the entire restaurant, so don't expect super quick service. Latin American countries are known for their slower pacing when it comes to meals as it is a family affair and not just grab-and-go. The staff knows our family but even if they didn't, they're all friendly (and bilingual, so don't be intimidated if you don't know Spanish). Highly recommend!

text: I brought my Corvette here as Charlie was highly recommended by other Corvette drivers in the city. While speaking with him I noticed his professionalism and level of knowledge . I had a bad steering rack and the car had also been in need of an alignment . I'd had the car 3 years and never had one done . The damage that was done was my fault and I had made the mistake of driving it as well and unbeknownst to me I was circulating particles through the power steering system. Charlie had my car picked up the morning I called him. I was not in a hurry and he'd gotten the car on a Friday so it was the next week when the diagnosis came in. As I already knew the rack and pinion was bad .The rack had to be ordered but I was told I could find a used one or a remanufactured one my own if I had wanted to but I let them do that because , in all honestly , I was having trouble finding one. Now I looked around online at how to do this myself as I have worked on my own cars off and on over the years. This is not an easy job particularly because of how the steering shaft and sensors can get all thrown out of whack and damaged if you do it wrong which would be more problems. There is almost no clearance under their either and the rack is in there really tight. It was after reading these articles and looking at it from under the car myself that I decided to call Clearview Auto . All work was performed and he was able to save my power steering pump by doing a thorough flush and adding an additive to help it ( My Corvette is 22 years old!) . He showed me the four wheel alignment specs that he did on my car and how far it had been out . On the drive home I could tell that it drove straighter and took turns much more decisively . He gave me a computer print out to save showing me all of this . Now Charlie drives Corvettes himself and has driven just about every model they've made from C1 all the way up to C7 and he knows a lot about them but he can work on any brand of car from what I can tell based on some of the cars I saw around his shop. In talking to him you realize he knows a lot more than the average person does about cars. He will not give you a quickie short cut repair job to make a quick buck and send you on your way I suspect. He has a very thorough and in depth approach when he explains the issues and why he suggests what your car needs in my experience. There are plenty of shade tree self taught mechanics out there if that's the route you want to go but modern cars and sports cars are too complex for that almost any more. Many older repair shops don't even have alignment machines or other special equipment now required and will send you to a tire shop for one . At this shop your car is in very capable hands and I will take my truck here in the future.

text: I was a bit worried when I came here. I mean when you come to a restaurant that is over 160 years old and you worry that you might not like anything on the menu. Especially when you still serve food on your menu that is original to the establishment. I pulled up my britches up and headed in, glad I did. Tujague's is steeped in history here, but seems to also be a well kept secret. When we showed up there weren't many in house, maybe it was early? We were greeted by the bartender and headed back to the seating area. Seated immediately and had menus in hand. A quick look over the drink menu, place a drink order, given some suggestions by our server, and we are off to the races. Our server was amazing. He was very knowledgeable about everything on the menu. Any question my party had, he knew the answer. He knew the history of the place and that the brisket recipe that was originally used is still in use to this day. Even though I kept looking over the menu, I kept coming back to the brisket. Knowing that the recipe is original made me keep telling myself, "You have to try it." And I did. Several people in my party decided to get an appetizer, I however decided to save room for the meal I had my mind set on. I stuck with the fresh bread brought to the table. One of my friends in the party got the oysters. These things were charbroiled. I am not one for oysters but they looked amazing and my friend, who was trying oysters for the first time, said they were delicious. Others in the party went with the Duck and Goat Cheese Crepes and Fried Green Tomato Ravigote. Both looked amazing and there were no complaints from any of them. Then out came the main courses. I can't tell you much about other people's food because I was focused on my meal. Tujague's Famous Brisket did not disappoint from a visual standpoint. The brisket it prepared boiled. This meant to me that it was going to be falling apart and flavorful. And it was. I felt like I needed to suck on the meat rather than chew. I was in heaven. The brisket was served over a bed of smashed Yukon golden potatoes. My god, those potatoes were dynamite. Loved the consistency, some clumps with the right amount of mashed, it was great. Then the Brussels sprouts, yum yum yum. They are cooked in bacon and onion, those things just sopped up the flavor. If you are brave enough, eat the brisket with some of the creole horseradish sauce. Just the right amount of kick to it to not overpower the bite. Price was a little up there, but for the meal I had I wasn't worried. I would gladly pay that price again. It hit the spot and we were taken care of like rock stars.

text: 4.5 It took me a while to get there but I finally got there: beets. They're not just for tasting like dirt and tricking you in to thinking they're delicious. Now, while you won't catch me biting into one of these things like an apple, I no longer recoil in horror at the very mention. I can take a *light* amount of them in a salad. I'll plop a gentle amount on my plate at a family-style seating. But, if they're on a juice menu, I'm all in. Luckily for me, Twenty Two Juicery knows their way around making some delicious beet juice. Their main beet attraction is the Can't Beet It. It's been on the menu since the beginning and there's a good reason for it: it's delicious. The combo is not especially unique but the execution is beyond reproach. I'm not kidding when I say that this was one of the best juices I've ever had. I don't know whether it's the ratio of vegetables to fruit. I don't know whether it was the freshness of the produce. But something happened in that juicer to turn beet, carrot, apple, lemon, and ginger into just the recipe to give me a healthy pep to my step and load me up with all sorts of important vitamins and nutrients. I suppose there's not too much more to say. Wait! There is! Okay, Twenty Two is located in the Indianapolis City Market. I went there around the holidays... at lunch time. Yeah. I know. But do *you* know that the folks behind the counter kept a smile on their faces, engaged in chit chat and banged those orders out in no time? Despite having a line, they kept things moving and got people where they needed to go when they needed to get there. A good product, a smile and a sense of urgency... I like it, Twenty Two. I imagine that the juice here should be on/in every Indy City Market patrons' rotation. If not, get on board. It's a new year. Health is wealth... and delicious.

text: It has now been a week since my horrific experience and I am still bothered by it. I have struggled with whether or not I would speak publicly about what I experienced and have come to the conclusion that I would share my experience in hopes that no one else would be subjected to such treatment. Saks Fifth Avenue has left me disgusted at the behavior that was displayed by employees who were specifically hand picked by management and chosen to represent their brand! Not only will I NEVER return, I will tell everyone that I know how this particular store treats their customers. On Saturday, April 6th at approximately 5:00 p.m. I was made to feel less than human as my race undermined my credibility in this high end retail store. While I was not wholly denied access, I was treated differently. In many ways, this a microcosm of racial exclusions embedded in American society. I am saddened and repulsed by the gross display of disrespect, disregard and overall rudeness that I endured at the hands of their employees. I will be graduating from a local university next month. I have worked hard and am proud of my accomplishments. As a reward, I decided to treat myself to a pair of high end shoes. Obviously, the first place that I thought of was Saks. My friend and I took the 20 minute drive to Frontenac to make the purchase. As soon as we entered the store (which was practically empty), the alarm activated. Being that we'd just walked in we both looked at each other with confusion and proceeded to walk to the shoe department. By now we notice two store clerks motioning to one another. While we were fully aware of their actions, knowing that we hadn't done anything wrong we continued to make our way to women's shoes. The female employee in the shoe department did not greet us. Meanwhile, I calmly and politely asked her if she could direct me to a particular brand of shoes. She then proceeded to ask me if I knew what size I needed. I explained to her that since the shoes are not American made, the size may be different. At no point did she direct us to an area with this particular brand. The saleswoman and I stood awkwardly face to face and in silence as she looked me up and down with pure disgust. While I was taken aback by her boldness, I chuckled slightly in disbelief. Did I smell? Was I not pleasant? Why was she interested in my appearance and not directing me to what I asked for? She finally responds with a snide grin and says, "Let me see what we have in the back!" Now I'm really confused. You're checking to see what's in the back? Other than me stating the brand of shoe that I was interested in, I stood patiently waiting to be directed to a display of shoes where I could choose what I wanted. What exactly was she checking for in the back? I didn't know exactly what I wanted, how could she? Maybe I was not privy to her physic abilities. That's it! She was able to read my mind! The salesperson returns literally within two minutes and says to us, "We don't have what you're looking for!" Oh! Now we get it! No need to say more! As we walked out of the store we see the other two clerks motioning to one another again. Extremely offended, my friend and I left the store shaking our heads in disbelief at what had just transpired. In closing, while I can't seem to forget the phrase, "We don't have what you're looking for!" out of my head, I still have faith in humanity. No one should ever have to feel belittled or less than because of the color of their skin. I suppose the folks at Saks didn't get the memo. Get on board people! This is 2019!

We had our boy with us, and any place with dog friendly seating gets the benefit of rounding up, unless everything else sucks, and it does not. Secondly, we met the owner while we were eating. Super-friendly guy, and I know a place doesn't deserve a good review just because the owner is a nice person, but it again, it provides more justification for the round up when the owner and staff are friendly and want to ensure you have a great experience. The food is what I was wavering on here. On the one hand, I liked what I ordered. On the other, I understand a couple of complaints about flavoring. The red chili sauce is not great. They give you the option of red or green - go green. Normally, red is my go-to; I will almost always go with the red chili sauce, red salsa, red hot sauce, etc. But at NuMex, always go green. It is much better. My burrito with the carne adovada - at the server's recommendation - was very good provided I was eating the portions with the green chili. The portions with the red were underwhelming. My partner felt the same about her veggie burrito. That said, we both really liked the chips and salsa. Salsa was excellent, and the chips were crispy and salty, my favorite! It would probably be a solid 4 stars had I went with green chili all the way, and an iffy 2.5 or 3 stars had I went red chili sauce. I was also disappointed in the lack of a full bar, but that is what it is. Not every place wants to pay for a full liquor license, but you'd think a mexican or southwestern restaurant would have a full bar and some specialty southwestern drinks. Not a reason to remove a star though - if I failed to look to see if they had a full bar and if that would have stopped me from going (it wouldn't have), then that's my fault. Since writing the above paragraphs, we've been back to NuMex. While I don't remember what I got - I remember liking my meal better this time. So I'm happy with the 4 stars. text: I waited 1 1/2 years from the day they installed my new heat pump to write this review. In January of 2018, one of the coldest days of the year, my husband came and woke me up. I had a surgical procedure the day before and was asleep. He told me our heat pump was broken and he had Donelson Air in our living room. I didn't get a good impression from the salesman when I met him. There was also another gentleman with him in one of their uniforms. The salesman told me they were having a sale on Rudd units. (I had never heard of this brand) He told me it would be about $9,000 for the new unit. I must say that was a shock. Our old one, a Trane, had cost $4,000 but that was 25 years before. 1/2 inside and the other outside split unit. I told him I wanted the whole house air purifier. "No problem," he said. To this day I do not know how much this whole house purifier cost us. I said to him that we had bought our old Trane heat pump from them 25 years before and how happy we have been with the unit and the installation of it. Our salesman 25 yrs before came and checked in on the workers every single day and came here a week later to make sure we were happy. We were so very happy!! So I mentioned that they would be replacing all of the ductwork as well. The man in the uniform told me in uncertain terms that "We do not do that". Ok. they sent 2 men in about an hour to install our new unit. The men told me most installers had been sent home and he and his son are the team that does commercial units. It took a long time. At one point the dad sat in the floor of the hall of my house reading installation instructions a long time. Finally, they finished and told me everything was fine and left. That night my husband mentioned that it was getting colder in the house rather than warmer. When he looked at the thermostat, it was way below sixty degrees so I called them. We paid cash for our unit and it wasn't working. I told them to either get someone out here or they could come and get their, non-working unit and give me my money back. They sent Aaron, who was a nice young man, and somehow he got it working. I would love to tell you that all was fine and I am thrilled but it didn't happen that way. The outdoor condenser unit sounded like a jet plane taking off. Every time it came on, the lights in our home would flicker. Then the unit would grind and make strange noises so we had them come again Couldn't find anything wrong and left. They sent Aaron and another young man a few days later since it was still sounding like a moose and the lights were still flickering. I had the flu. The boys were here all day. That afternoon I told them I had to go to bed. 102 temp. They said ok, we will lock up when finished. I woke up and there was a receipt for the work with the words that the customer was happy with the results. I kept calling until no one there wanted to talk to me. Our dear salesman never once reached out to us in any form. I left a message to the General Manager one day but he never returned my call. Finally, they sent a man from the Rudd company. They had put it in backward. We are talking weeks here by this time. He said it was now working and all would be fine. No, it wasn't. I guess the unit running for months turned backward messed it up. Finally, in April, they agreed to put in a new condenser. They did and left. Do you remember that whole house air purifier? The one I do not even know how much it cost? It wasn't making sense to me. My furniture was always covered in dust again every morning. I kept telling my husband that it wasn't working right. I knew it was a good one because the man from the codes department told me that they "Fixed you up good"! So why was I still coughing and dust everywhere in my house? I will tell you why. They didn't replace the 25 yr old duct work. This unit is more efficient and it continues to blow dirt, dead skin cells, pet dander, mold spores and anything else that was in that ductwork for 25 years. I am stuck with a condenser that is a jet plane. And an air purifier with lamps that are supposed to burn off any kind of dirt and germs. Those bulbs must be replaced every year or two they said. It isn't working because the stuff is in the duct work. It isn't air coming from the basement to run through the air purifier. We will tell everyone we ever meet that Donelson Air is very good at ripping people off. I never want anyone else to go through what we have. If you are looking for a company to replace your 25 yr old heat pump just keep going right past this name!! If you need an air purifier, I have one that doesn't work for me that you can have. Oh, the salesman that first morning told us this unit will last between 10-12 years.

text: Panorama, unfortunately, joins the ranks of the many bars and restaurants that constantly discourage me from going out for mass-produced events such as Restaurant Week or any other Prix Fixe event. I went to Panorama for Valentine's Day where they offered a prix fixe menu that sounded like it was going to be great. Unfortunately, we were thoroughly disappointed with a number of things. Firstly, the food was just ok. One would hope that a restaurant would make enjoyable food their first priority. And with a Prix Fixe menu of $60/plate you expect to put down your fork and say 'wow that was good'. I ordered the lobster bisque which had one lonely slab of lobster-chunk sinking into an ectoplasm of mediocre milky sea-floor funk. My date ordered the elk fusilli dish. I would tell you it was forgettable, but I forgot about it so quickly that I question whether a flavor even entered my brain to begin with. My date ordered a Negroni which was actually quite lovely. I ordered the Pear Sidecar which was so lacking of pear flavor and so cruelly alcohol-forward that I probably would have gotten more use out of it by pouring it into a car engine. Admittedly, the homemade focaccia with pesto was awesome. This was certainly the highlight. Serendipitously one of the waiters brought us over multiple breads accidentally and well, I wasn't complaining. Now at this point we waited. 35 minutes, then 40, 45, 50.... and finally 55 minutes later from when we finished the first course, and after both the tables adjacent to us (who had arrived significantly later than us) received and finished their entrees... we received our cold entrees! I ordered the lamb and my date ordered the veal braciola. All I will say is thank god both dishes were relatively tasty as I was ready to walk out at this point. This was made worse by the fact that we had no idea who our waitress was (probably went through at least three of them, but wouldn't know for sure because they didn't introduce themselves). Regardless, no apologizes for our wait. No information about when our food would arrive. Didn't check back to see how the cold food was. And worse yet, when we tried to order wine (which is the main export of this place) the waitress could not provide us any information about our choices except that they were all... in fact... wines. Truly enlightening stuff. For a place that calls itself a wine bar I expect a little more. She also recommended the neighboring table get a Negroni. They asked her what was in a Negroni to which she replied bourbon and then proceeded to grab the menu from the customer and read the correct ingredients aloud. Finally, the desserts were, for lack of a better and less scathing word, terrible. The olive oil cake was offensive on the pallet with a strange lemony taste and no discernible essence of olive oil. The tiramisu was one of the worst I've had. Needless to say we did not finish our desserts. If you hate having extra money in your bank account and want to waste your date and your stomach's time, go to Panorama for your next fancy dinner.
label: NEG
